title: TracePoint run event
description: One line of events.ndjson, and of the stream produced by --events. The file is append-only and each line is a complete JSON object, so a reader can tail a live run. Events are ordered by seq, which starts at 1 and never repeats within a run. A reader must ignore event types and data fields it does not recognise: new types are added in minor versions.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number within the run, starting at 1.

t_ms.description: Milliseconds since the run's monotonic start. Negative before load begins, as during preflight.

wall.description: Wall-clock time of the event, for display and log correlation only.

type.description: What happened. run.finished is always the last event of a completed run and carries the digest.

data.description: Payload, shaped by type. Shapes below are the guaranteed fields; more may be added.
Run parameters, fixed for the run.

seed.description: Seed actually used, whether configured or drawn.

runners.description: Runner names and kinds taking part.

config_hash.description: SHA-256 of the effective, redacted configuration.

data.description: A bucket closed and was reduced to its summary. Emitted once per runner per bucket; the main progress signal for a live reader.

index.description: Bucket index from the run start.

insufficient.description: True when n is below run.min_samples, meaning this bucket is displayed but not used as evidence.

warmup.description: True when the bucket falls inside warm-up.

rps.description: Completed operations per second in the bucket.

data.description: An incident began or ended. Class is provisional while open and final when closed.

class.description: Incident class; see the result schema for meanings.

end_s.description: Seconds from run start, on close.

culprit.description: Best-ranked culprit, when one can be named.

data.description: A capacity-search level. Emitted only by capacity runs.

level.description: Level index, in the order tried.

phase.description: Where the level came from: doubling, refine or confirm.

ok.description: Whether the level held its SLOs, on completion.

achieved_rps.description: Measured throughput in the steady window.

p99_ms.description: Measured p99 response time in the steady window.

data.description: Something a human should know that did not stop the run: a degraded validity finding, an unavailable telemetry sampler, a deprecation.

code.description: Stable warning code, from the same registry as error codes.

data.description: Terminal event. Carries the exit code and the full digest, so a reader consuming only the event stream never has to open another file.

exit_code.description: Process exit code the run resolved to.
